content: Neonatal malaria is an extremely rare condition, even in regions where malaria is endemic. The transmission of malarial parasites from mother to child typically occurs during the process of delivery, a phenomenon known as vertical transmission. Globally, malaria continues to impose a significant health burden. It is estimated to cause over 300,000 fetal and infant deaths annually, as well as approximately 2,500 deaths among pregnant women each year. Malaria during pregnancy can lead to several severe complications, including premature labor, intrauterine growth restriction, high perinatal mortality, maternal anemia, miscarriage, and low birth weight in newborns.
